  {
   "t": "Process",
   "b": "p23"
  },
  {
   "t": "Paradigm",
   "b": "p23"
  },
  {
   "t": "Participants",
   "b": "p4"
  },
  {
   "t": "Presentation",
   "b": "doc"
  }
 ],

}
</script>
</div>

::: {#exr-03-purpose-statements-that-work-interactive}
## Purpose statements that work, interactive

Select the purpose statements that have a problem, an owner and a so-that. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="pick">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "options": [
  {
   "t": "to study why developers ignore security warnings so that tooling can be redesigned",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "to identify onboarding steps where password-manager users abort, so that the client can prioritise fixes",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "to look into cyber security in companies",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "to make the client's website better",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "to prove that TypeScript reduces bugs",
   "ok": false
  }
 ],
 "explain": "A purpose statement is one sentence: to (find out X) so that (Y benefits). \"Prove\" presumes the answer; \"better\" is a goal, not a purpose.",
 "ref": "sec-03-purpose",
 "reflabel": "Purpose"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-03-the-funnel-interactive}
## The funnel, interactive

Click the stages of the funnel in order, from the widest to the narrowest. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="order">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "steps": [
  "Topic",
  "Problem",
  "Purpose",
  "Research question"
 ],
 "explain": "A topic is a broad area of interest; a problem is something wrong, unknown or needed with an owner and a cost; the purpose says what the study will find out and for whom; the question follows.",
 "ref": "sec-03-purpose",
 "reflabel": "From topic to problem to purpose",
 "hint": "click the stages, widest first"
}
</script>
</div>
```

::: {#exr-03-research-or-standards-interactive}
## Research or standards?, interactive

Two systems of knowledge production: sort each property to the system it describes. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "res",
   "label": "Research"
  },
  {
   "id": "std",
   "label": "Standards and practice"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "Descriptive, explanatory claims",
   "b": "res"
  },
  {
   "t": "Prescriptive, normative claims",
   "b": "std"
  },
  {
   "t": "Validation by evidence, replication, peer review",
   "b": "res"
  },
  {
   "t": "Validation by consensus, voting, uptake",
   "b": "std"
  },
  {
   "t": "Generalisation is the aim",
   "b": "res"
  },
  {
   "t": "Applicability is the aim",
   "b": "std"
  },
  {
   "t": "Failure means the hypothesis is rejected",
   "b": "res"
  },
  {
   "t": "Failure means the standard is not adopted",
   "b": "std"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Standards are normatively binding without having been tested empirically; research generalises and corrects itself by refutation.",
 "ref": "sec-03-two-systems-of-knowledge-production",
 "reflabel": "Two systems of knowledge production"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::
